✅ tz (timezone) hardening done (Sweep_Engineer) — root cause found & fixed, suite verifiably green.

Diagnosis: the whole suite was ALREADY green (322 passed), but two real tz-robustness gaps existed in confirmation.py matching the reported TypeError class:
1. All-NaT dtype trap: when a frame has ZERO confirmations, pandas builds `confirm_df["confirmation_time"]` as naive `datetime64[ns]` — and `pd.Series(x, dtype="datetime64[ns, UTC]")` silently FAILS to upgrade a naive all-NaT column (verified in isolation), so the column stayed naive while the candles index was tz-aware → consumers comparing `confirmation_time` against the index hit "Cannot compare tz-naive and tz-aware" (TypeError).
2. Mixed-tz lookups: `get_indexer([confirmation_time])` / `get_indexer([event_time])` raised TypeError when the passed value's tz-awareness differed from the candles index.

Fix (src/events/confirmation.py):
- confirmation_time is now normalized with `pd.to_datetime(..., utc=True)` (+ `.tz_convert(index.tz)` for aware indexes, `.tz_localize(None)` for naive) — naive values are read as UTC per the new documented *timezone policy* (module docstring): aware index → aware UTC values (matches schema §6 `datetime64[ns, UTC]`), naive index → naive values, all-NaT/zero-confirm keeps the index's tz-awareness.
- All timestamp→bar lookups (`_event_position`, confirmation-time lookups in build_entry_schedule / compare_entry_strategies) go through `_lookup_position` + `_as_index_timestamp`, which normalize the searched value to the index's tz-awareness — mixed tz-naive/tz-aware input can no longer raise TypeError (naive treated as UTC).

Tests: +3 regression tests in tests/test_confirmation.py — tz-naive candles full flow (attach/schedule/A-B compare) consistent & TypeError-free; zero-confirm keeps tz-aware dtype; mixed tz (naive timestamps against aware index, and vice versa) resolves to the correct bar instead of raising.
